_resolved: The community vacancy test did not complete for W force-matched and Li switched UG; the same calculation done directly (one-vacancy cell, atoms and cell relaxed together from a 1e-3 A rattle) gives 2.98 eV (fixed cell 3.13) and 1.02 eV (fixed cell 1.03) with the bcc crystal intact, so neither is a collapse and neither is listed. Cr switched UG and V force-matched were redone the same way: Cr's perfect crystal stays bcc, but with a vacancy and the cell free it turns close-packed (2 % of atoms keep the bcc first shell, median coordination 11) and E_V comes out at -345 eV (the community test, by another path, -85); V's perfect crystal itself leaves bcc once the cell may relax (75 % of atoms lose the bcc first shell, 5.5 % denser, 0.055 eV/atom lower), so its -52 eV is not a vacancy energy.
_source: Independent tests, run 2026-11-01..03 on a separate implementation of the potential (a model driver written for this check, not part of this release) with community test code, switched and re-cut sets only (a hard cut makes the energy discontinuous). open_collapse: a prototype outside fcc/hcp/bcc/dhcp that relaxes, cell free, more than 0.5 eV/atom BELOW the fitted structure - energies no metal has; dE in eV/atom relative to the fitted structure. vacancy_cell_free: the vacancy test, which relaxes the cell as well, where it returns a negative energy (eV) or does not complete. The library's own vacancy energies are at fixed cell (lammps/vacancy.py) and are not these.
